messages.author: 7c80fc81c3454752
messages.subject: A model for double responce
parts:
Hi,

I'm currently modeling two types of response, one is beta and another is binomial. 

I have 15 counties as random effect for the whole state.

For the beta response, I have 76 observations and for the binomial response, I have 84 observations.

The covariates for the beta are x_1, x_2 and x_3. For the binomial is just x_1.

Is it possible to use the iid2d in inla to model this?

messages.author: 7c80fc81c3454752
messages.subject: Re: A model for double responce
parts:
This is a pseudo model I built without correlation random effect, and it works as I expected. Is there any way to include the correlation?

Y <- matrix(NA, ncol = 2, nrow = 76+84)
Y[1:76,1]<-sb18$propDriver[sb18$propDriver<1]
Y[77:160,2]<- ifelse(sb18$propDriver<1,0,1)

inla(Y ~ logvmt+road+road2+one_2+logvmt2 + f(county,model = "iid")+f(county2,model = "iid") ,
               family = c("beta", "binomial"),
               data = data.frame(Y = Y,
                                 logvmt = c(log(sb18$Vehicle.Miles.Traveled[sb18$propDriver<1]),rep(NA,84)),
                                 road= c(Road,rep(NA,84)),
                                 road2= c(Road2,rep(NA,84)),
                                 one_2=c(rep(NA,76),rep(1,84)),
                                 logvmt2 = c(rep(NA,76), log(sb18$Vehicle.Miles.Traveled)),
                                 county = c(as.factor(sb18$County[sb18$propDriver<1]),rep(NA,84)),
                                 county2=c(rep(NA,76), as.factor(sb18$County))
                                 ))

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] A model for double responce
parts:
that should go fine yes, assuming the iid2d dependency is in the latent field.
some reponses are missing it seems but that will not create an issue.

the better parameterization is the new iidkd model, see the documentation for
details.
